claims.text: Aristotle tutored Alexander the Great, hired by Alexander's father, Philip II of Macedon.
Plato, Socrates and Pythagoras did not tutor Alexander the Great.

Aristotle studied at Plato's Academy in Athens for about 20 years.

evidence.restatement: Philip II of Macedon engaged Aristotle as tutor to his son Alexander.
Socrates died in 399 BC and Pythagoras around 495 BC, before Alexander was born in 356 BC, and Plato never taught him.
Aristotle went to the Macedonian court around 343 or 342 BC to teach the young Alexander.
